children: How the National Stock Exchange of India's trading debut goes will depend heavily on market sentiment, says Apurva Sheth at Samco Securities. The debut comes against a backdrop of rising bond yields headlined by the U.S. 10-year crossing 5%, which is generally negative for equities. But Sheth notes that the NSE IPO was priced significantly below the levels at which it was trading in the unlisted market, so he expects the stock to list at a premium. Post-listing, he sees the chances of a major fall below the issue price as relatively limited. Even if a large portion of retail investors sell in the first hour or two, that should be absorbable by the market, Sheth adds, noting that roughly 35% of the issue size was reserved for retail investors. (fabiana.negrinochoa@wsj.com)
